script.title: Cash vs Accrual Basis of Accounting
script.caption_hook: Rent unpaid, yet it's in the books? That's accrual basis.

lines.say: Ma'am, I haven't paid December's rent, but accounts still show it?
Yes, that's accrual basis. Cash basis records when money moves. Accrual records when the right or duty arises.
So what's the difference in numbers?
Say rent is ₹10,000 a month. You paid eleven months, ₹1,10,000. December is unpaid.
So what's the rent expense for the year?
Cash basis says ₹1,10,000, only what you paid. Accrual says ₹1,20,000, all twelve months incurred.
Then where does the extra ₹10,000 go?
It's outstanding rent, a liability. Accrual shows such dues and prepaid items. Cash basis ignores them.
Is there a formula for the expense?
Accrual expense equals paid plus closing outstanding minus closing prepaid, when no opening dues. Here ₹1,10,000 plus ₹10,000 is ₹1,20,000.

board.title: Accrual expense
board.sub: Closing items only; no opening dues assumed

lines.say: Where do I see both bases together?
In non-profits. Receipts and Payments Account is cash basis. Income and Expenditure Account is accrual basis.
Remember: cash basis, when cash is received or paid. Accrual, when earned or incurred.

Checker: Line 4/5 (example setup): the script never says the accounting year ends on 31 December. Indian students usually think of an April–March financial year, and under that year an unpaid December rent would not be outstanding at year-end. Suggested wording: 'For the year ending 31 December, rent is ₹10,000 a month. You paid eleven months, ₹1,10,000; December's rent is still unpaid.' The arithmetic is correct: ₹10,000 × 11 = ₹1,10,000, and ₹1,10,000 + ₹10,000 = ₹1,20,000.
Checker: Line 12 flow board: the labels 'Receipts' → 'Income' are cut short. Use the full names: 'Receipts & Payments A/c' → 'Income & Expenditure A/c'.
Checker: Line 13 board: the slash spacing is inconsistent ('received / paid' vs 'earned/incurred'). Make both the same, e.g. 'Cash: received/paid' and 'Accrual: earned/incurred'.
